newsitem.title: USA: DuPont to invest $1.7 billion in Pioneer Hi-Bred.
newsitem.headline: DuPont to invest $1.7 billion in Pioneer Hi-Bred.

text.p: DuPont Co. will invest $1.7 billion for a 20 percent stake in Pioneer Hi-Bred International as part of an alliance that includes the formation of a joint venture to develop new crops, the companies said Thursday.
After a delayed opening following the news, Pioneer's stock leaped $17 to $93.75 on the New York Stock Exchange shortly after midday.

As part of the agreement, under which DuPont will pay $104 for each share of Pioneer, it will have two of the 15 seats on Pioneer's board of directors, the companies said. Pioneer will use the proceeds to buy back its own stock.
The agreement includes a 16-year standstill and corporate governance agreement, the companies said.

"This linkage with DuPont will enable Pioneer, as an independent company, to team with a leading agricultural technology provider to meet the changing needs of crop producers and end-users of grain and oilseeds," Pioneer Chairman Charles Johnson said in a statement.

The equally owned joint venture company will be called Optimum Quality Grains. It will include DuPont Agricultural Products' Quality Grains business and Pioneer's Nutrition Industry Markets business, both based in Des Moines, Iowa.

The companies said the alliance will create one of the world's largest private agricultural research and development collaborations. The two will collectively invest more than $400 million in agricultural research next year.

A portion of those budgets will support the joint venture directly, with collaborative research in genetic modification of corn, soybeans and other oilseeds to improve their oil, protein and carbohydrate composition.
Both companies can also apply discoveries and technology gained from the alliance to enhance their traditional products, such as hybrid seeds and crop protection products.

DuPont said it expects to take a one-time, non-cash charge against its earnings of up to $1 billion as part of its investment in Pioneer. The charge is to write off research and development that is in process.
In addition to its biotechnology-based business, DuPont Agricultural Products also supplies crop protection products, which are not part of the alliance.

The alliance between Pioneer, the largest North American seed corn company, and DuPont follows similar ventures in the growing area of agricultural biotechnology. DeKalb Genetics Corp., the No. 2 seed corn company, has an alliance with Monsanto Co., which has a significant minority stake in DeKalb.
